newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.6 vs 11.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.6 vs 11.2 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate rose 40 basis points to 11.6 percent on Thursday despite modest demand, thanks to a larger volume of term loans.
Daily trade amounted to 29.4 million kuna, with a shortfall of two million in demand, against 60 million on offer.
Fresh settlements totalled 22.6 million kuna, more than half of which were call money borrowings at a steady 10.5 percent.
Interbank term rates ranged between 9.40 percent charged by one foreign bank for an 11-day loan and a maximum 16 percent for one-month funds.
Insurers rolled over previous one-week loans at nine percent and one smaller one-day loan at 16 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Friday weaker at 6.0533 versus the dollar and slightly stronger at 3.5694 against the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
